headline: Spheria maintains Santos position at 7x FY26 EV/EBIT, viewing the post-Iran peace deal share price weakness as an attractive entry into a growing cash flow story
reasoning: Santos is Australia's second-largest independent oil and gas producer with a low-cost, long-life upstream portfolio anchored by LNG across Australia, PNG, Timor-Leste and Alaska. Management targets an all-in free cash flow breakeven of US$45–$50/bbl and aims to return at least 60% of FCF to shareholders from 2026, with Barossa LNG and Pikka Oil projects expected to lift group output by ~15–27% in 2026. Shares fell in June following confirmation of a US-Iran peace framework which removed the geopolitical risk premium from oil prices. However, Spheria believes ongoing regional instability reinforces the importance of energy security and diversifying supply away from the Middle East, enhancing the strategic value of Santos's portfolio. quote: Santos (STO AU) - is Australia's second-largest independent oil and gas producer, with a portfolio spanning LNG, domestic gas, crude oil and condensate across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and Alaska. Santos operates a low-cost, long-life upstream portfolio anchored by LNG, with interests in PNG LNG, Gladstone LNG and Darwin LNG providing exposure to Asian gas demand alongside domestic Cooper Basin and Western Australian supply. Management runs the business to an all-in free cash flow breakeven of US$45 to US$50 per barrel and targets returning at least 60% of free cash flow to shareholders from 2026. Its Barossa LNG and Pikka Oil (Alaska) projects are ramping up and are expected to lift group output by roughly 15% to 27% in 2026, moving Santos from a heavy capital investment phase into stronger cash generation. The shares fell during June following confirmation of a peace framework between the United States and Iran, which removed much of the geopolitical risk premium from oil prices and in turn weighed on Santos. Nevertheless, we believe that ongoing regional instability reinforces the importance of energy security and the need to diversify energy supply away from the Middle East, enhancing the strategic value of Santos's portfolio. Santos trades on 7x FY26 EV/EBIT, a multiple that should look increasingly attractive as Barossa and Pikka reach full production.

reasoning: Bapcor fell 25% in May and was a major detractor. A mid-month profit downgrade was driven by significant wage inflation, elevated oil and fuel prices, and weak car servicing demand. quote: Bapcor (BAP) experienced a weak performance in May, exacerbated by a profit downgrade announced mid-month amid deteriorating macroeconomic conditions. This is a complex situation that requires conviction. Significant wage inflation, elevated oil and fuel prices, and their adverse impact on car servicing activity and product demand have created a challenging operating environment. The balance sheet is still under repair, which is limiting capital flexibility and potentially requiring divestments in what remains a buyer's market. That said, several positive elements are emerging. The macro headwinds are expected to moderate over time, and the new CEO, Chris Wilesmith – an experienced aftermarket parts executive from Supercheap Auto – has made an encouraging start to the turnaround since joining in December. Early sales data prior to the US-Iran conflict, together with positive feedback from our supplier discussions, point to improving momentum under his leadership. The Trade division, representing approximately 35% of group sales, remains the standout asset. We estimate it generates revenue of around $800m and, at a conservative mid-cycle EBIT margin of 10%, this business alone – operating in an effective duopoly with Repco (GPC) – is worth in excess of $800m and potentially more than $1 billion. This compares to BAP's current EV of only $450m. The retail brands present a more challenging turnaround, although initial signs of market share gains are evident in the mid-May release. Potential divestment of selected wholesale and specialist businesses would provide further scope for debt reduction. Pro-forma net debt of $195m following the equity raising has already declined to $168m. Chris is successfully attracting talent back into the organisation, and we view him as the pivotal factor in the recovery. Given its attractive Trade platform, Bapcor also presents as an obvious target for private equity or a strategic buyer such as US-listed O'Reilly Automotive (~$75 billion market cap), which is a close mirror image of the group in the US market.

headline: Spheria maintains position in SiteMinder despite 29% share price fall, viewing it as a net AI beneficiary with strong growth prospects
reasoning: SiteMinder fell 29% during February despite producing strong first-half results — organic revenue grew 23% and recurring SaaS revenue grew 27%, and the business generated cash flow for the first time since its 2021 IPO. Spheria attributes the sell-off to broad negative sentiment toward software companies rather than fundamental deterioration. The firm views SiteMinder as a net beneficiary of AI, serving as the central execution and optimisation layer across the global hotel ecosystem with 20+ years of proprietary data providing a durable moat. It remains the neutral connector to 400+ channels, which booking engines and agents cannot independently replicate. quote: Siteminder produced a strong set of first half results. Organic revenue grew 23% with the recurring SaaS component up an impressive 27%. The business also broke well and truly into cash flow generation mode - the first time since it IPO'd in late 2021. Normally the market would have cheered such a result however the prolific sell-off and derating across software companies since the beginning of the year saw the share price retrace on negative sentiment. SiteMinder has sought to position itself as a net beneficiary of AI, with customers using its platform to streamline service, cut costs, and improve efficiency. Serving as the central execution and optimisation layer across the global hotel ecosystem, it synchronizes inventory, pricing, and distribution in real time with 100% accuracy. Its moat comes from 20+ years of proprietary data across thousands of hotels, channels, and countries, which it leverages to power AI features that are both deterministic (executing and displaying information) and probabilistic (forecasting demand and optimising pricing). As AI drives further fragmentation through new channels and agents, SiteMinder remains the neutral connector to 400+ channels, enabling hotels to make fast, optimised decisions that booking engines and agents cannot replicate independently. We are not stubbornly unaware of the AI disruption threat across the broad technology sector however, we currently hold the view that a limited number of tech franchises will retain enough competitive advantage to be relevant in a new AI world order. Siteminder has a net cash balance sheet, is cashflow breakeven and trading on ~3x FY26 EV/Revenue with currently exceptional growth prospects ahead of it.

headline: Spheria holds and modestly adds to Hemnet despite persistent weakness, arguing real estate portals are harder to disrupt by AI than feared
reasoning: Hemnet, the dominant Swedish real estate portal, has been a significant detractor since peaking in February 2025. Weakness is attributed to a softening Swedish housing market, concerns about market dominance, competitive position erosion, and fears that AI chatbots will disrupt network effects. Additional headwinds arose from Google testing a new mobile real estate advertising format. Despite this, Spheria has added modestly to the position, arguing that real estate is a high-stakes transaction where buyers cannot afford to miss listings and sellers cannot afford to miss buyers. Hemnet has 70-90% direct and organic traffic, strong brand, and is developing its own vertical AI features. Less than 1% of traffic currently comes from AI chatbots, and agents benefit greatly from the status quo, reducing the likelihood of voluntary disruption. Spheria acknowledges AI as a genuine risk but concludes real estate portals will likely prove harder to disrupt than markets fear.
quote: Despite the obvious uncertainty attaching to this question, we remain holders of HEM and have added modestly to the position in recent months. Our thinking is as follows: Real estate is a 'high stakes' transaction. Transacting in a property is often the biggest transaction of the buyer and the seller's lives. The buyer cannot afford to miss any listings in their search, and the seller cannot afford to miss any buyers, as the cost of doing so could dwarf the cost of the listing. HEM is developing vertical Ai features. To the extent that the risk to the business is an app that sits inside ChatGPT and the other Ai chatbots, HEM seems highly likely to be that app. HEM has high brand recognition, with very high (70-90%) levels of direct and organic traffic flows, evidence of embedded agent and consumer behaviours and habits. Today well less than 1% of HEM's traffic comes from Ai chatbots. If this grows and prospective buyers wish to begin their purchase journey on an Ai chatbot, HEM will be part of that in the same way that it uses Google as a marketing funnel today.

headline: Spheria holds overweight in USLM and would add further on share price weakness, citing highly favourable industry structure and strong cash generation
reasoning: USLM is an integrated manufacturer of lime and limestone products with owned long-life quarries and mines, serving primarily steel manufacturing and construction markets. The lime industry is highly regionalised, with USLM and competitor Lhoist together serving the central US and Texan markets, creating a duopoly-like structure that supports strong cash flows and returns. In Q3, strength in construction tied to large data-centre projects is offsetting weakness in oil and gas services volumes, and price growth remains robust at +5%. Spheria views USLM as a high-quality business operating within a highly favourable industry structure and states they would gladly add further to the position should the share price continue to soften materially from current levels.
quote: USLM is a highly cash generative, high returning business with a net cash balance sheet. As is almost always the case, it's the industry structure that's decisive in giving rise to these characteristics. Specifically, the lime industry is highly regionalised, with its heavy, low value per tonne nature making it costly to transport long distances. Consequently, there tends to be 2 or 3 primary competitors in each region, as is the case with USLM & its main competitor, Lhoist, which together serve the central US and Texan markets. Whilst competing sources of lime (from say, Mexico) do find their way into the market from time to time, not only is the landed cost higher but there's also a quality trade-off. So as long as USLM (and Lhoist) don't abuse their privileged market position, the opportunity to continue to generate strong cash flows and returns should persist long into the future. USLM is a high-quality business operating within a highly favourable industry structure. We will gladly add further to the position should the share price continue to soften materially from current levels.

quote: Sapiens International Corporation (SPNS US) has long been a core top 10 holding in the portfolio. It operates in a large and growing addressable market of $40b+ pa, with only half of the 2500 global insurers having migrated off their inefficient (20yo+) legacy core systems. At 11.5x EBITA and with a net cash balance sheet, we argued that the stock was simply too cheap as the market extrapolated the present into perpetuity despite the transient nature of the pressures along with the steps management was taking to address them. Notwithstanding the share price 'breather' during the month, this has been an outstanding investment for the Fund since we first started buying it in January 2023 at CHF21.58 per share (vs last CHF69.75/sh). In that time, the stock has delivered a total return equating to 60%pa compound, making it the largest positive contributor to the Fund's performance. ACLN now trades on 21x EBIT, having materially re-rated over the past 3yrs. We think this is justified by the quality of the business and the step-change in growth. headline: Sapiens International (SPNS) bid for by private equity at 64% premium, validating Spheria's thesis that the stock was too cheap at 11.5x EBITA
reasoning: Spheria had defended its holding in SPNS following share price underperformance, arguing at 11.5x EBITA and with a net cash balance sheet the stock was simply too cheap as the market extrapolated transient headwinds into perpetuity. SPNS is a global software business with 40+ years of experience powering global insurance companies, operating in a $40b+ addressable market with only half of 2,500 global insurers having migrated off legacy core systems. Revenue growth had stalled due to macroeconomic weakness, competitive pressures in the US P&C market, and accelerated pace of cloud migrations. Advent International agreed with Spheria's assessment, launching a board-supported takeover at a 64% premium over the August 8th closing price. The stock was the largest contributor to performance in August, rising 55%.
quote: Last month we put forward a strident defense of the Fund's holding in SPNS following a period of share price underperformance. This month the stock delivered strongly for unitholders after it was bid for by private equity. As a reminder, SPNS is a global software business with 40+ years of experience in developing and implementing software and customer engagement platforms that power global insurance companies. It operates in a large and growing addressable market of $40b+ pa, with only half of the 2500 global insurers having migrated off their inefficient (20yo+) legacy core systems. At 11.5x EBITA and with a net cash balance sheet, we argued that the stock was simply too cheap as the market extrapolated the present into perpetuity despite the transient nature of the pressures along with the steps management was taking to address them. As it transpired, global private equity player Advent International agreed with our assessment, launching a board-supported takeover at a 64% premium over SPNS' August 8th closing price.

headline: Spheria defends overweight in Sapiens despite near-term revenue growth slowdown, citing 30% upside to mid-cycle valuation at just 11.5x EBITA
reasoning: Sapiens is a global insurance software business operating in a $40bn+ addressable market, with only half of 2,500 global insurers having migrated off legacy systems. Organic revenue growth has slowed from a consistent 6-9% to near zero due to macro-driven customer deferrals, increased US P&C competition, and a near-term revenue drag from cloud migration of existing clients converting licence payments to annuities. Spheria believes this is a transitory period: the company is integrating AI to differentiate, expanding cross-sell and L&A focus, and building system integrator channels. Cloud delivery will ultimately improve business quality via more recurring revenue, lower support costs, and automatic updates. At 11.5x EBITA with a net cash balance sheet, Spheria sees 30% upside to its through-the-cycle valuation.
quote: We believe the market is being short-sighted and that this will transpire to be a transitory period of low growth for SPNS. Firstly, the company is responding to the competitive challenge in the US, actively integrating Ai into its product to differentiate itself, expanding cross-sell initiatives (most customers only have 1 product), enhancing the focus on L&A (where competition is less intense) and it continues to build out system integrator partnerships globally as an entirely new channel to market for the group; Secondly, whilst the transition to the cloud impacts near term earnings, ultimately business quality improves dramatically as cloud delivered software means more recurring revenue (improved financial stability and valued highly by the market), lower support costs, whilst the customer simultaneously reduces its IT hardware spend and receives automatic updates; and Lastly, the macroeconomic uncertainty will pass, as it always does. SPNS now trades on just 11.5x EBITA, has a net cash balance sheet, and offers 30% upside to our fundamental, through the cycle valuation.

headline: Spheria retains Accelleron as a core holding after a 50%+ rebound, viewing it as fairly priced at 19x FY26 EBITA but well-supported by execution, balance sheet strength and multiple tailwinds
reasoning: Accelleron is the Swiss-based global leader in off-highway turbochargers for merchant marine and energy markets, with a mission-critical product that reduces fuel consumption and emissions. Over 50% of revenue comes from the merchant marine sector and 75% of group revenue is from servicing the existing fleet, providing resilience against short-term trade disruptions. The stock rebounded over 50% from tariff-related lows partly due to tariff negotiation progress and the strengthening Swiss franc (which benefits the company translationally and transactionally given ~50% of revenue is in CHF). Additional tailwinds include new IMO climate regulations from October 2025 and datacentre demand for backup and baseload power. At 19x FY26 EBITA the stock is seen as fairly priced but the company is gaining share, broadening its product suite, and generating phenomenal cash flow and returns.
quote: With the benefit of hindsight this would have been a great buying opportunity, with the stock rebounding over 50% since that time to make new highs. The reasons for this appear to be twofold. Firstly since 'Liberation Day' (2nd April), markets have breathed a long and collective sigh of relief as the US approach to tariff negotiations has inclined towards compromise. Over 50% of Accelleron's revenue comes from selling turbochargers and associated services to the merchant marine industry, so a reduction in global trade would clearly be unhelpful for the business. Having said that, the shorter-term impact would be modest given 75% of group revenue comes from servicing the existing fleet of turbochargers and the shipyards are book through at least 2027-28, meaning that turbocharger deliveries for newbuilds will continue regardless of short-term trade trends. The other factor driving Accelleron's recent bounce is the strength of the Swiss franc. Around 50% of its revenue negotiated, priced and settled in Swiss francs, which has rallied ~15% off the lows from earlier this year. As the company reports in USD, this will benefit the company from both a transactional and translational standpoint. Further, in April the IMO (International Maritime Organisation) announced a tightening of its climate regulations from October 2025 where fleet owners with aggregate emissions in excess of a predefined limit must pay into the IMO's Net Zero Fund. This, along with datacentre demand for both backup and baseload power, provide further tailwinds for Accelleron's business. Following the recent rally the stock is looking more fairly priced at 19x FY26 EBITA. Having said that the company is executing well, outperforming ours and the market's expectations as it gains share in turbochargers and broadens its product suite into new and growing TAMs. The balance sheet is strong and its cash flow and returns are phenomenal, and as such it remains a core holding in the Fund.

headline: Spheria adds to Hemnet position on 25% price decline, viewing regulatory concerns as overstated and valuation highly attractive at 26x FY26 EBITA.
reasoning: Hemnet's share price declined 25% during the quarter and over 30% from its February peak, driven by a weak listings environment and concerns from the Swedish Competition Authority and Real Estate Agency Inspectorate over market dominance and agent remuneration. Spheria views these concerns as overstated: 9 out of 10 Swedish homes were advertised on Hemnet in 2024, unchanged for five years, and no formal investigation has been confirmed. The fund sees Hemnet as early in the journey of rebalancing value capture away from agents toward the portal, and notes that forced removal of agent commissions could actually boost earnings. Following the selloff, the stock trades at 26x FY26 EBITA, which Spheria considers very attractive for a market-leading portal with strong network effects, strong cash generation, and capital return via dividends and buybacks. Spheria used the weakness to add to the position.
quote: Following the recent sell-off, the stock trades on an FY26 EBITA multiple of 26x, which is very attractive for a market leading real estate portal with strong network effects, generating strong cash flow and returning capital to shareholders via dividends and share buybacks. We are strongly of the view that the amount of value captured by real estate portals versus real estate agents is grossly disproportionate in favour of the agents and that Hemnet is very early on the journey of rebalancing this equation. The Real Estate Agency Inspectorate concerns over Hemnet's agent remuneration structure may perversely be a positive for the company. It is our view that the strength of Hemnet's network effects is such that there's little need to pay agent commissions, so having them forcibly reduced or removed would boost earnings without impacting market share.

headline: Spheria adds to Hemnet on a 25% quarterly share price decline, viewing regulatory concerns and weak listings as transient and not material to long-term valuation
reasoning: Hemnet operates the dominant online real estate portal in Sweden with over 40 million monthly website visits and 16x more listing clicks than its nearest competitor, making it the default platform used by nearly all real estate agencies. The share price declined 25% in the quarter and more than 30% from its mid-February peak, driven by a weak listings environment (June listings -9% yoy) and concerns from the Swedish Competition Authority and Real Estate Agency Inspectorate over its market dominance and agent remuneration structure. Spheria does not expect these issues to have a material impact on Hemnet's valuation in the long term, noting no formal investigation has been confirmed by either regulator, and has used the weakness as an opportunity to add to its position.
quote: Hemnet operates the dominant online real estate portal in Sweden, connecting property buyers, sellers and real estate agents on the one platform. The company was founded in 1998 and by the 2000's had become Sweden's default property marketplace with listings from nearly all real estate agencies flowing to the site, making it a high traffic, high trust platform. Today Hemnet garners >40m visits to its website per month and 16x more clicks on listings than its nearest competitor. Hemnet's share price declined by 25% during the quarter and is down more than 30% from its mid-February peak. This is partly due to a weak listings environment, with June -9% yoy. The sell off also comes on the back of concerns expressed by the Swedish Competition Authority over Hemnet's market dominance and the Real Estate Agency Inspectorate over Hemnet's agent remuneration structure. No formal investigation has been confirmed by either group. Longer term, we do not expect these issues to have a material impact on Hemnet's valuation. Thus we have used the share price weakness as an opportunity to add to the Fund's position in the stock.

headline: Spheria remains optimistic on Eagle Materials at 11x EBIT, citing high-quality low-cost assets, structural supply tightness, and bipartisan infrastructure spending tailwinds.
reasoning: Eagle Materials is a US manufacturer of cement and gypsum wallboard with operating margins and returns consistently above 20%, driven by vertical integration into low-cost lime and gypsum mining reserves. Synthetic gypsum supply has structurally tightened as US coal-fired power plants have more than halved in the past decade, reducing a key alternative input. On the cement side, regulatory burdens and community resistance make capacity additions rare, keeping supply and demand finely balanced. Bipartisan support for large public infrastructure spending should drive cement demand growth over the next 2-3 years, while a rebound in single-family home construction as interest rates ease should spur gypsum wallboard demand. Despite this quality, Eagle trades at a very modest 11x EBIT, which Spheria considers far too cheap, and they remain happy and optimistic holders.
quote: Eagle Materials is a US manufacturer of heavy construction materials, primarily cement and gypsum wallboard. On the face of it this might sound like a dull and commoditized business where you'd expect to find high levels of competition and little scope for excess returns. One look at Eagle's financial accounts tells you that you'd be mistaken, with operating margins and returns both consistently north of 20%. A number of factors give us confidence that this can be sustained or even improved upon. Firstly, Eagle is vertically integrated into both the mining of lime and gypsum, where they have the advantage of long-life, low-cost reserves. These inputs ensure the cost-competitiveness of their manufacturing plants versus much higher cost imports. Secondly, gypsum supply has structurally tightened in recent years, with synthetic gypsum – previously a viable alternative to natural gypsum – having dwindled in availability with the number of US coal-fired power plants more than halving in the past decade. Similarly on the cement side, capacity additions are a rarity owing to a burdensome regulatory environment and a reluctance from local communities to host new cement plants in their neighborhoods. All of this means that supply and demand are finely balanced for Eagle's key products, with future demand increases likely to translate directly into commensurate increases in price and margins. On the demand side, bipartisan support for large public infrastructure spending should fuel growth in the demand for cement over the next 2-3yrs, whilst a rebound in single-family home construction as interest rates ease will ultimately spur gypsum wallboard demand. With one of the highest quality (low cost) portfolios of assets in the building materials space that we've come across, Eagle currently trades on a very modest 11x EBIT. This is far too cheap, and we remain happy and optimistic holders of the business.

quote: Wise is a disruptive global technology company that is building out the infrastructure to facilitate money transfers and provide multi-currency accounts to individuals and businesses. Wise is transforming the markets in which it operates, displacing slow, expensive and opaque offerings from large banks. Over two thirds of cross-border transfers are still done through the banks, providing ample scope for continued market share gains. Wise's competitive advantage lies in its infrastructure, with its 850+ software engineers and associated staff who together are responsible for establishing the in-country connections and licensing that helps to drive its cost and speed advantage. In addition, Wise management is intelligently executing somewhat of a 'land-grab' strategy by passing the benefits of its scale back to its customers in the form of reduced prices. This underpins the group's rapid growth, which in turn lowers its unit costs and further drives growth. By way of example, 50% of Wise's current transaction volume is facilitated by moving money between Wise customers, whereby the money doesn't actually leave the country, thus reducing execution costs. The bigger Wise gets, the more this percentage will increase, the greater its competitive moat. We continue to be attracted to Wise's net cash balance sheet, double-digit rates of revenue growth, and its more than reasonable earnings multiple of ~20x PBT.

The stock has re-rated to ~US$220/share (19x EBIT), but remains attractive. Check Point has 30+ years of client relationships, over 100,000 clients, offices in 88 countries, and founder/chairman Gil Shwed holding 23% of shares. FY24 results showed 6% revenue growth with strong cash conversion and US$1b of buybacks. Revenue growth is expected to continue in the mid-to-high single digit range with over US$1b of annual buybacks, and its simple unified security solution is in strong demand as cyber needs grow in scope and complexity.
quote: Check Point is one of the leading players in the global cyber security software market. It has been protecting its >100k clients for 30+ years and possesses deep local market expertise with offices in 88 countries. It's founder and chairman, Gil Shwed, holds 23% of the shares in the company. In February, Check Point delivered a solid FY24 result, with 6% revenue growth and strong cash conversion. The company bought back $1b of stock and maintained a net cash balance sheet. The Fund initiated its position in Check Point in late-calendar year 2023 when it was trading below US$150/shr equating to 14x EBIT. The stock has been a stellar performer, now trading just shy of US$220/shr or 19x EBIT. The investment thesis was predicated on the company's technological strength, long-standing reputation, and comprehensive security approach. We were also able to capitalise on the market's excessive focus on the CEO transition and associated risk that the new CEO would materially rebase margins in a bid to drive greater top line growth. Despite the re-rating, Check Point remains an attractive investment and continues to deliver strong operating performance, with revenue growth in the mid-to-high single digit range and is buying back north of US$1b of stock every year. Customer needs in the cyber security space continue to grow both in scope and complexity, with Check Point's simple and unified solution in strong demand.

headline: Spheria sees elevated Australian equity volatility in March driven by unsustainable valuations and market crowding into winners

They note US government spending cuts will hurt the US economy short-term but could lead to a more sustainable economic footing if tariffs and lower tax rates incentivise private sector investment. They expect the market will eventually look ahead to a recovery. The fund's focus on cashflow, balance sheet and valuation has supported performance during the rotation away from expensive growth stocks.

headline: Spheria warns that momentum has driven small-cap markets away from fundamentals and valuations, but expects a reversion to fundamentals-driven performance
reasoning: The past year saw momentum strategies triumph over fundamental investing in the small-cap market, with stocks experiencing earnings growth bid up with little regard for valuations while cyclical or downgraded businesses fell sharply. The firm remains steadfast that cash flow generation and disciplined valuation will drive long-term outperformance and sees parallels to prior periods when momentum reversed.
quote: The past year marked another year where momentum largely triumphed over logic. The small cap market was marked by a significant uplift in the stocks with earnings growth with scant regard to valuations. Correspondingly, businesses with earnings cyclicality and downgrades plumbed new lows. With apparently fewer investors looking to fundamentals - just ask an ETF or index fund what multiple their underlying investments are trading on – it shouldn't be surprising that things have somewhat disconnected from the economic laws of gravity. Just as a law is a law and not an opinion, however, our view on the weighing ability of the stock market longer term remains intact. Whilst momentum has been the friend of some this year, we have seen the momentum engine slow and reverse previously and have a strong sense of déjà vu.

headline: Spheria's top holding CarGurus rallied +36% in December quarter on strong earnings; remains attractively valued at 17x ex-wholesale EBIT
reasoning: CarGurus is a US online automotive marketplace connecting buyers and sellers of new and used cars, gaining market share in a competitive three-player US market. The stock returned +36% in the quarter following a strong Q3 result that beat expectations on both revenue and earnings, driven by pricing and strong adoption of new dealer efficiency products. CARG is generating ~15% pa top-line growth well ahead of cost growth, resulting in 50%+ earnings growth, and is materially outperforming competitors like Cars.com. Spheria met with management in September 2024 and was impressed by CARG's cheaper pricing, 20% more inventory and 50% more traffic versus competitors. Trading at 24x FY25 EBIT on face value, excluding the loss-making wholesale business (where losses are reducing) brings the multiple to 17x, which Spheria views as very attractive for a share-winning marketplace with net cash and strong cash flow.
quote: CARG is a US online automative marketplace that connects buyers and sellers of new and used cars, much in the same fashion as CarSales (CAR AU) operates in the Australian market. Unlike the Australian market, the US is more competitive, with three major players of roughly equivalent size. CARG has been gaining share and trades at an attractive valuation given the potential for this to continue. The stock returned +36% during the quarter on the back of a strong third quarter result. CARG outperformed market expectations on both revenue and earnings, with pricing the main driver, underpinned by strong adoption of new products that improve dealer efficiency as well as ongoing annual pricing reviews. CARG is generating top line growth of ~15%pa, well in excess of cost growth, resulting in earnings growth of 50%+. Importantly, CARG is materially outperforming its competitors, with Cars.com reporting a comparatively lackluster result for the quarter. The Spheria team met in person with CARG management in September 2024 (along with a key competitor) and came away impressed. What stood out was that CARG offers cheaper pricing than competitors, has 20% more inventory and 50% more traffic, all of which translates into a much better ROI for its dealer customers. Further, the company's obsessive focus on innovation was evident, helping dealerships run their businesses better and be more profitable. CARG is now the largest holding in the fund, reflecting both our conviction in the name and the stock's strong level of outperformance. Trading on a prima facie multiple of 24x FY25 EBIT, CARG doesn't look especially cheap. But excluding the loss-making wholesale business (in which losses are reducing) brings the multiple down to 17x. This is very attractive for a marketplace business that's winning share, generating strong cash flow and has a net cash balance sheet.

headline: Spheria is underweight the US market due to inflated valuations, stock-based compensation distortion, and a benchmark with 63% US weighting
reasoning: Spheria highlights that the MSCI World Small Cap benchmark has a 63% US weighting, making a benchmark-weight allocation imprudent without compelling relative value. The US market trades at a 40-70% premium on forward P/E relative to Japanese, European and UK markets. Additionally, widespread reporting of profits on a pre-SBC basis materially flatters headline multiples, making the US appear cheaper than it truly is — in many cases SBC consumes the entire reported profit. Trump's re-election was seen by markets as net positive due to business-friendly policies, but Spheria is cautious about selective market interpretation of his policy mix. On balance of probabilities, Spheria expects some valuation convergence across regions over the medium term.
quote: So why is the fund underweight the US market? The first thing to highlight is the unusually high weighting in the benchmark to US names. At 63%, a benchmark-weight allocation to the US market would necessitate that two out of every three stocks we owned be domiciled in that market. Whilst the US economy has a lot going for it, such a significant allocation seems imprudent on the face of it, absent compelling value relative to alternate markets. Stock-based compensation (SBC) is a sensible means of aligning employees with shareholders. But make no mistake, it is a real cost for the business. The issuance of stock merely substitutes what was formerly a cash payment of salary for equity dilution. We know of many companies whose entire reported profit is more than consumed by SBC. This has the effect of obscuring value unless one digs into the accounts to understand discrepancies between 'underlying' and statutory results. It also means that headline multiples are significantly flattered, making the US market appear cheaper than it actually is. Even with this unfair advantage, the US market trades at a material premium, ranging from 40% to 70%, on a one-year forward P/E basis relative to the Japanese, European and UK markets. We are the first to acknowledge the limitations of a PE ratio and that expensive assets can always get more expensive. But on the balance of probabilities, we expect some convergence in value across regions over the medium term.

We believe that the value of a security is a function of the future free cash flow that it generates. Those that buy cash burning businesses presumably do so for one of two possible reasons... For every Amazon (which notably lost money for 9 consecutive years before turning its first profit in 2003), there are many many more WeWorks. Spending one's time searching for the proverbial needle in the haystack makes little sense to us in the context of an investment universe that's so vast (~8000 companies) and rich with businesses that have observable track records of profits and cash flow. Focusing on businesses with observable track records of generating cash flow and with sound balance sheets tilts the long-term odds in our investors' favour and may just be the closest thing to a free lunch that's available in the global small cap market.

headline: Spheria maintains conviction in Zillow despite NAR settlement headwinds, arguing the likely impact on revenue is minimal and longer-term structural upside remains significant
reasoning: Zillow underperformed after the National Association of Realtors announced a US$418m settlement designed to promote more transparent buyer-agent commission structures. Spheria believes the most likely outcome is little to no impact on Zillow's revenue, noting that 13 states have already operated under a similar model with no observable impact. Fewer commission dollars could actually make Zillow more valuable to productive agents, driving up lead prices. Longer term, Spheria sees potential for the US to shift from a lead-gen to a paid-inclusion model similar to REA Group in Australia, with Zillow capturing more of the economics. On a market cap per capita basis, Zillow would be worth 26x more than its current price if valued like REA Group, though Spheria acknowledges this is not its base case.
quote: Whilst this may negatively impact the aggregate size of the agent commission pool (from which Zillow's earns its revenue), the most likely outcome in our view is little to no impact on Zillow. Notably 13 states have operated for a few years under a model similar to what's proposed under the settlement, with no observable impact on Zillow's revenue. Indeed, fewer dollars to go around for buyer's agents could actually make Zillow more valuable for the most productive agents, driving up the price of leads. Longer-term, there is some prospect that these changes ultimately pave the way for US to move from a 'lead-gen' to a 'paid inclusion' model like the one that we see in Australia, with the role of aggregating buyers shifting from the buyers agents to Zillow, in turn allowing Zillow to capture more of the economics. Whilst not our base case and the following analysis is admittedly crude, on a market capitalization per capita basis, Zillow would be worth 26x more than the current share price were it to be valued like REA Group (REA.AX).

reasoning: Star Entertainment's share price fell 34% in September following a deeply discounted capital raising that was partly pre-empted by the market. headline: Spheria trimmed Smartgroup after strong outperformance but remains attracted to its EV-driven novated leasing growth profile

At its Q1 update, Smartgroup reported strong lead volume growth of +31%, with EV quotes comprising over 20% of total novated leasing quotes and a healthy vehicle order pipeline of $16m. Novated leasing benefits from pent-up demand from COVID-era supply chain constraints unwinding and from new FBT exemption legislation for EVs and hybrid vehicles.

Reflecting this, SIQ's vehicle order pipeline sat at a healthy $16m, and novated leasing yields were up +3% versus the prior corresponding period. Thus, with rising interest rates and cost of living pressures crimping demand in most corners of the economy, novated leasing demand remains robust, benefiting from pent-up demand as covid related new vehicle supply chain constraints gradually unwind, as well as growing tailwinds from the introduction of new legislation abolishing FBT on EV's and hybrid vehicles. Having acquired the stock <$5/share, SIQ has been a strong performer for the fund. At current levels the value equation is more balanced than it was, but we remain attracted to its growth profile, consolidated industry structure, strong cash flow profile and minimally geared balance sheet.

headline: Dominant global cinema software and analytics provider; market undervaluing SaaS transition potential which could lift recurring revenue 3-5x; net cash, approaching structural free cash flow positivity from late CY24
reasoning: Vista Group's share price bounced hard off May lows as investors warmed to its prospects as the dominant software and analytics provider to the global film industry. Full year results showed 38% revenue growth and free cash flow moving into positive territory. The company is transitioning clients from on-premise to cloud/SaaS, which requires significant upfront investment but will increase recurring revenue 3-5x versus current maintenance license revenue and create significant positive operating leverage. Vista has over 50% global market share by screens (excluding China), a net cash balance sheet, and is expected to move structurally into free cash flow positive territory from late CY24. The market is not ascribing sufficient value to the potential SaaS-like nature of the revenue combined with Vista's industry dominance.
quote: Vista Group (VGL NZ) – The share price has bounced hard off its May lows as investors warm to the prospects of this dominant software and analytics solutions provider to the global film industry. Vista delivered its full year results in March, with revenue growing 38% and free cash flow moving into positive territory after several challenging years due to COVID restrictions on cinemas. In addition, the company continued to deliver on its strategy of transitioning clients from on premise to the cloud (i.e. SAAS) which has required significant upfront investment by the company. Once complete, this transition will increase recurring revenue by 3-5x versus current maintenance license revenue and result in significant positive operating leverage for the business and commensurate free cash flow generation. We don't believe that the market is ascribing sufficient value to the potential SaaS like nature of the revenue in combination with VGL's dominance of the cinema industry. Vista has >50% market share by screens globally (excluding China). The business has a net cash balance sheet and marginal cash burn this year before moving structurally into positive territory from late CY24.

quote: Global AI has gained a lot of attention of late, with investors (and speculators!) on the lookout for the next Nvidia. There are not many ways to get leverage to AI in the Australian listed market outside of Appen and with a refreshed management team already making inroads as demonstrated at the investor day in May we are confident of what lies ahead for this business. Appen is well placed to benefit from the growth in generative AI which requires human input, particularly as it relates to ensuring the accuracy of the outputs. Appen has been pivoting towards Large Language Model (LLM) type work with the expectation that this market will grow to more than $100bn by 2030. The recent capital raise provides ample funds to invest in the growth of the business for the next couple of years. A substantial US$300m of revenue (admittedly vs a peak of around >US$400m) alongside a re-engineered cost base will mean the business achieves profitability in the short to medium term. On a price to revenue metric the company is trading on less than 1x. Assuming the business can generate 10% EBIT margins (not a stretch in our view) it would be generating US$30m of EBIT and trading on a modest 10x EV/EBIT.

Appen is well placed to benefit from the growth in generative AI which requires human input, particularly as it relates to ensuring the accuracy of the outputs. Appen has been pivoting towards Large Language Model (LLM) type work with the expectation that this market will grow to more than $100bn by 2030. The recent capital raise provides ample funds to invest in the growth of the business for the next couple of years. A substantial US$300m of revenue (admittedly vs a peak of around >US$400m) alongside a re-engineered cost base will mean the business achieves profitability in the short to medium term. On a price to revenue metric the company is trading on less than 1x. Assuming the business can generate 10% EBIT margins (not a stretch in our view) it would be generating US$30m of EBIT and trading on a modest 10x EV/EBIT.

headline: Portfolio construction skewed to ~70% net cash balance sheets as protection against cyclical downturns and to preserve optionality to acquire over-geared competitors near cycle troughs
reasoning: The fund holds approximately 70% of its positions in companies with net cash balance sheets. The rationale is that debt is the only mechanism through which a company can go bankrupt, so a strong balance sheet protects against being forced out of positions during cyclical downturns. Additionally, net cash positions provide optionality at cycle troughs to acquire over-leveraged competitors or invest organically to widen competitive moats. Excessive leverage is particularly dangerous when combined with weak competitive positioning and regulatory dependence, as illustrated by the US regional bank failures. The strategy is designed to reduce the impact of losses on performance and tilt the playing field in favour of long-term investors.
quote: Across the fund, around 70% of our holdings have net cash balance sheets. Debt is not inherently 'bad'. Indeed the application of leverage can improve the process of capital allocation across an economy, resulting in a net gain in productive investment. In addition, the benefits and risks of leverage are symmetrical, with the magnification of returns a feature on the positive as well as the negative side of the ledger. However, it's at the individual company level where the reasons for our scrutiny on the balance sheet come into focus. The benefits of a strong balance sheet can be summarised as follows: You can't get 'stopped out' by a cyclical downturn in operations. The only way a company can go broke is if it has debt; and - Optionality – At or near the bottom of the cycle, this may include the ability to buy over-geared competitors and/or to invest organically in the company's own operations as a means of widening its moat.

headline: Zero weighting to US regional banks — structurally disadvantaged by scale economics, weak risk controls, and fragile regulatory moats; leverage ratios of 10-20x made collapse inevitable
reasoning: The fund has no exposure to US regional banks, which contributed over 100bps of outperformance in March as the sector fell 18%. The US banking market has over 4000 FDIC-insured commercial banks, making it highly competitive and fragmented. Competitive advantage in banking accrues to scale, placing regional banks at a structural disadvantage. Softer regulations that attempted to level the playing field also weakened risk controls, and combined with rising rates and concentrated lending to cash-strapped crypto and tech borrowers, led to the collapse of SVB, Signature and Silvergate. Leverage ratios of 10-20x amplified all of these vulnerabilities, resulting in a particularly poor risk/reward for investors.
quote: US regional banks fail to meet our investment criteria on multiple fronts. The US banking market is highly competitive and fragmented, with >4000 FDIC-insured commercial banks as of December 2022. Competitive advantage in banking is typically a function of scale, with lower funding costs and superior unit economics accruing to the larger players in the industry. By definition this places the regional banks at a disadvantage to their larger peers. Softer regulations were an attempt by US regulators to level the playing field. Weaker risk controls (aided by the softer regulatory requirements), rising interest rates, and a concentration of lending activities to cash-strapped segments of the economy (crypto and tech) all contributed to what was a spectacular collapse. Dependence on regulation to sustain a company's niche can be a fragile moat at the best of times. But leverage ratios in the range of 10 to 20:1 combined with the abovementioned factors gave rise to a particularly poor payoff for investors, in our view.

headline: Strong buy on recurring cellular revenue inflection, school safety tailwinds, mandatory fire alarm upgrades and copper network decommissioning; no debt and strong cash flow despite non-cheap earnings multiple
reasoning: Napco's competitive advantage stems from its culture of innovation (dozens of patents) and vertically integrated end-to-end solutions across alarms, locking and access control, delivering superior reliability. A key inflection 7-8 years ago saw the company capitalise on copper phone network decommissioning by introducing a $10-$25/month recurring cellular signal-transmission fee routed through its own NOC. Revenue is 80% commercial and 20% residential, distributed globally through wholesale distributors. Growth drivers include increasing school safety focus, regulatory mandated fire alarm upgrades, and ongoing copper obsolescence, all of which support high-value recurring revenue. quote: A key inflection point for the business occurred 7-8 years ago when Napco seized on the looming decommissioning of the copper phone networks to introduce a recurring revenue product to its suite. Historically the signal from Napco's products (alarm, fire etc) was transmitted through the telecommunication provider's copper networks to a central station, where the appropriate authorities were notified, and the appropriate course of action taken. With the decommissioning of the US copper networks, Napco's cellular radio-capable products now route the signal to the central station via Napco's own Network Operations Centre (NOC). For this service, the company receives a $10-$25/month fee. Whilst the stock is not outright cheap on earnings multiples, it has strong cash flow and returns, no debt, and continues to be well-placed to benefit from several growth drivers, including the increasing focus on school safety, regulatory mandated fire alarm upgrades, and copper phone line obsolescence, which will help to drive high value recurring revenue for signal transmission over Napco's cellular infrastructure.

quote: Hemnet (HEM SS) – As Sweden's largest real estate portal, Hemnet has greater than 10x the revenue and monthly visitation than its nearest competitor, making it more dominant than the leading portals in the USA, UK, Germany and Australia. Evidence abounds of how hard it is to dislodge a market leading real estate portal. Like any marketplace, volume begets volume. Indeed the network effects are arguably more powerful for real estate portals than for the average marketplace given that buying a home is one of the most significant financial transactions that the end customer will ever make. This characteristic lend itself to a winner-takes-all/most industry structure, as the cost (perceived or otherwise) of not advertising where the most eyeballs reside can be significant. Like most of the markets we look at, Swedish home buyers are retreating in the face of higher interest rates, with Hemnet reporting a 10% decline in fourth quarter listing volumes vs the prior corresponding period. Notwithstanding this, listing price increases in excess of 30% are helping to deliver revenue growth and higher margins. This is an unusually stark demonstration of a company exercising its pricing power. For context, Hemnet is relatively early on the journey of monetising its dominance, evidenced by comparatively low listing prices (both in absolute terms and as a percentage of house prices) in comparison to other market leading real estate portals. With a capable management team, a board populated by ex-Realestate.com.au and ex-Rightmove executives, and its sheer dominance, we remain confident in the long-term prospects of this business.

headline: Bullish on global microcaps as a superior risk/return asset class versus large-caps, particularly given stretched valuations and market concentration reminiscent of the dot-com era
reasoning: Spheria argues that global microcaps not only enhance returns but can reduce overall portfolio risk, especially in the current environment of excessive valuation and risk-taking. Historical evidence across the dot-com bust, GFC, and COVID shows microcaps fell only marginally more than large-caps in drawdowns but recovered significantly faster — for example, during COVID the MSCI World Microcap Index was up 18.4% in USD by the time the MSCI World Index had merely returned to pre-COVID levels. Spheria attributes this outperformance to microcaps being more nimble in cutting costs and securing liquidity, the asymmetric manufacturing cycle favouring microcaps in recoveries, and the fact that selling in crises concentrates on larger, more liquid companies. They see current stretched valuations and market concentration as classic dot-com hallmarks and expect microcaps to outperform on any downturn as they did on the way up.
quote: However, over time, we have amassed evidence that indicates, not only should global microcaps enhance investors' returns, but they could do this while reducing overall portfolio risk. Especially now, where like many experienced market observers, we see signs of excessive valuation and risk-taking. We expect that when this bull terrier market (bull terrier because it won't let go) ends, our global microcap Fund will likely outperform its larger peers on the way down too (it has already outperformed on the way up).

headline: Extreme valuation multiples on high-growth stocks carry asymmetric downside: a 5% growth shortfall or a 1% rise in discount rates destroys a disproportionate share of investor capital versus fairly-priced peers
reasoning: The fund argues that stocks priced on very high multiples, such as Shopify, are far more sensitive to forecast errors and interest rate changes than lower-multiple peers like Channel Advisors. A 5% reduction in assumed growth rates causes investors to lose roughly half their money in the high-multiple stock, while the impact on the lower-multiple stock is far smaller. Similarly, a 1% increase in the discount rate has a much larger negative effect on the high-multiple stock. The fund emphasises that the risk to rates is asymmetric — rates cannot fall much further without embracing negative rates, but they can rise significantly from current low levels. The conclusion is that managers buying at extreme multiples must be prepared to answer difficult questions when fundamentals reassert themselves.
quote: We don't cover Shopify, it's too large for us. It may grow by the requisite 12.4% using our simple framework, and it may grow by a lot more. But hopefully, we have shown that if managers are buying shares on extreme multiples, they better be prepared to answer some difficult questions when fundamentals return to the fore. We aim to find great companies, but a large part of the puzzle always lies in the price we pay for an asset. We are not buying shares for what someone might pay for that same share tomorrow. We are buying shares for the future stream of cash flows that will accrue to minority shareholders. It's boring, but it's all been done before.

reasoning: Spheria went back and analysed the top 10 performing microcaps in each of the past 7 years and found that well under 50% of the top 10 made money over ensuing 2-year-plus timeframes, with 8 or 9 of the top 10 often losing money. Flipping the analysis, the subsequently best performing microcaps over a 10-year period showed that 9 out of 10 were money-making, with consistent growing earnings, cash flows and sustainable durable businesses. The firm argues for working with probabilities rather than improbabilities and views cash flows as the beating heart of any great long-term business.
quote: We went back and analysed the top 10 performing microcaps in each of the past 7 years to see whether the Sturm und Drang surrounding the best performing short term names proved warranted over time. In most of these years well under 50% of the top 10 made money and in many 8 or 9 of the top 10 names lost money. headline: Top detractor but holding conviction; share price implies margins halve, yet trades on 13x FY21 P/E with 6.5% dividend yield and EPS growth of 14% p.a. to FY23 — all negatives seen as transitory
reasoning: Fjordkraft is suffering from poor investor sentiment triggered by a negative broker report, with concerns around consumer contract disclosure scrutiny, competition from smaller players offering switching incentives, and an equity raising overhang. The company's expansion into Sweden and Finland shows higher margins in those markets, and consensus FY21 P/E of 13x with a 6.5% dividend yield and EPS growth from 3.69 in FY20 to 5.46 by FY23 (14% p.a.) make the valuation compelling.

Meanwhile, EPS is forecast to grow from 3.69 in FY20 to 5.46 by FY23, or growth of 14% p.a. Our thesis remains that regulatory changes and consolidation by Fjordkraft will improve the industry structure and help maintain margins above expectations. Significant back-office synergies from expected future acquisitions further aid this.

headline: Parts of the microcap market are over-extended on retail fervour; pockets of investor disinterest remain in areas with temporary earnings lags or perceived lack of growth, offering valuation opportunities
reasoning: Retail investors have returned to the market with fervour, pushing certain areas — especially in microcaps — to levels that are hard to justify on fundamentals. However, pockets remain where there is complete investor disinterest, chiefly in areas with temporary earnings lags or where sectors are not perceived as high growth or disruptive. The fund continues to adhere to valuation discipline as the best way to serve investors over the cycle, particularly if inflationary forces cause longer-term interest rates to continue rising.
quote: Little over the past few months has allayed our concerns that parts of the market are over-extended. Retail investors have rushed back into the market with fervour. This has pushed areas – especially in micro caps – to levels that are hard to justify on fundamentals. Oddly however there remain pockets of market where there is complete investor disinterest chiefly in areas where there are temporary earnings lags or there is a perception that the sectors are not high growth or disruptive. Should inflationary forces return on a more permanent basis longer term interest rates may continue to rise. We continue to believe adhering to a valuation discipline with this backdrop is the best way to serve our investors over the cycle.

headline: Not owned; positive contributor as it fell 10% when NdPr oxide prices dropped ~25% from March highs; rare earths are not scarce and high prices will incentivise new supply, undermining massive valuations on potential producers
reasoning: Lynas was not held by the fund and its retracement contributed positively to relative performance. Spheria acknowledges strong EV and wind turbine demand for Neodymium-Praseodymium oxide but notes vehicle and turbine makers are actively spending to reduce or eliminate usage through substitution (e.g. low-temperature superconducting magnets for turbines, switched reluctance motors for EVs). More fundamentally, rare earths are not actually rare, and current prices are well above incentive levels for new supply, meaning several potential producers are likely to raise capital and move into production over the medium term, diluting the investment case.
quote: While we acknowledge the growth in EVs and wind turbines (the key end markets for this material) should be very strong we also note that vehicle and turbine makers are spending considerable funds to reduce and / or eliminate the usage of this material through substitution with alternate materials and / or technologies (e.g. Low temperature superconducting magnets in the case of turbines, switched reluctance motors in the case of EVs). More fundamentally we would note that rare earths are not actually very rare. The current extremely high price for this material is well above the incentive price required to induce new supply growth. The massive valuations being ascribed to potential producers is likely to see several raise sufficient capital to move into production over the medium term.

headline: MMT and ultra-low rates have inflated asset prices; inflation may not be dead and the self-induced economic coma is being over-stimulated, creating pockets of over-hype in micro/small caps alongside genuine opportunities

Microcaps in particular have exploded off the bottom with the most speculative names reaching new heights. The fund is cautious on the most overinflated areas but sees pockets of attractive opportunities that have not attracted the fickle attention of the market.

Precisely how a supposedly scarce resource (money) suddenly being made not scarce cannot have an impact on its value is a bit of a quandary. Although MMT adherents believe that inflation really is dead – simply because it has been dormant for a long time – the same certainly cannot be said for asset prices. Whilst we would be cautious on the most overinflated areas of the smaller companies space, there continue to remain pockets of attractive opportunities which we believe have not attracted the fickle attention of the market.

headline: Largest detractor (-10%) on softer-than-expected result driven by refinancing mix and COVID savings rates; still trades at ~8.5x annualised EBIT with strong housing finance tailwinds expected to drive greater operating leverage in 2H21
reasoning: Mortgage Choice was the largest detractor, falling 10% following a result that disappointed expectations. At c.8.5x annualised EBIT, the stock still looks lowly priced given favourable mortgage finance tailwinds.

The book growth was also hurt by the staggering COVID-19 lift in savings rates which saw loan balances paid down and cash held in offset accounts (trail is paid on net balances outstanding). headline: Hold with conviction despite recent lag; regulatory unbundling drives consolidation tailwinds, strong balance sheet, and Norway's hydro system limits power price spike risk
reasoning: Fjordkraft is Norway's leading electricity retailer, formed in 2001, and has been a top holding for some time. The company benefits from Norway's large hydropower system (half of Europe's hydro-reservoirs), which blunts electricity price spikes because 75% of national production capacity is flexible. New legislation effective 1 January 2021 requires unbundling of Distribution System Operators from retail operations, making electricity retailers the sole player with end-customer relationships and spurring industry consolidation. Fjordkraft is participating in this consolidation, improving industry structure and capturing cost synergies. After strong performance through COVID into September, the stock has lagged as risk-on sentiment bypassed this low-risk, high-quality compounder. The Fund remains invested given valuation support, a strong balance sheet, and an improving industry structure.
quote: Secondly, there are regulatory tailwinds supporting retailers. Legislation which came into effect 1 January 2021 requires legal and functional unbundling of Distribution System Operators (DSOs) from other operations. Thus, electricity retailers will be the only player in the electricity value chain with an end-customer relationship... Fjordkraft is participating in this consolidation. The acquisitions act to improve the industry's structure and Fjordkraft benefits from the cost synergies of combining these businesses which operate large administrative centres. After some solid performance through covid and into September, the company has lagged the broader microcap market over the past few months. It is not surprising that this high quality and low-risk company has been shunned in the latest round of risk-taking by market participants. Nevertheless, with valuation support, a strong balance sheet, and improving industry structure, our Fund remains contently invested.

headline: Vaccine-driven rotation from long to short duration (growth to value/cyclicals) is underway, but the empirical link between rising real yields and value outperformance has broken down since the early 1990s, making the rotation less predictable than theory implies
reasoning: The fund discusses how equity portfolio positioning has been dominated by macro duration factors since Covid, with long-duration (growth) strategies outperforming as real yields fell. Positive vaccine news is now prompting a rotation toward short-duration (cyclical/low P/E) stocks, consistent with expectations of an economic rebound, higher inflation and rising interest rates. However, the fund notes that while the long-run theory favours value in a rising-rate environment, the empirical relationship has been unreliable since the early 1990s; in recent years growth has actually outperformed value even as real yields rose, complicating any straightforward duration-based rotation call.
quote: Duration, spreads and convexity. Not terms uttered by equity managers in a typical day. However, the share market has been dominated by macro factors since Covid. Equity managers are increasingly turning into bond investors. Whether they are long or short duration has been the overriding factor behind their relative performance. Going long duration means your portfolio benefits more than the Index if interest rates fall. In equity terms, this is equivalent to owning more growth stocks. Since growth stocks have more of their earnings in the future, they are more sensitive to interest rates and their impact on the rate those cash flows are discounted back to present value. As interest rates fall, so too does the discount rate, and future cash flows are worth more in today's dollars. With positive vaccine news, investors are beginning to position short duration (as are bond investors). That is that interest rates will rise and future cash flows will be worth less in present terms. Under this scenario vaccines will underpin a robust macroeconomic rebound, stoking inflation and lifting interest rates. Cyclical stocks and those on low price to earnings, where more of the earnings are near-dated, will do best in this environment.

headline: Valuation disparities at dot-com boom levels: low rates justify higher valuations for proven high-growth businesses, but not for unproven models with uncertain cashflows; deteriorating demographics and low wage growth make earnings growth more uncertain
reasoning: The fund argues that while low long-term interest rates should ceteris paribus lead to higher valuations, the reasons for the long-term decline in rates — deteriorating demographics, low wage growth and persistent failure of inflation to hit central bank targets — suggest earnings growth is more uncertain than previously. It therefore makes sense to pay more for high-returning, high-growth businesses with strong barriers to entry and proven models, but not for highly uncertain cashflows from unproven business models. The fund prefers 'boring' but proven, cash-generative names trading well below their historical relative trading ranges.
quote: With the rise of passive, quantitative and now direct retail investors in the market it is little wonder valuation disparities appear to be at levels not seen since the dot.com boom. While we don't dispute that low long term interest rates that are currently being seen ceteris paribus should lead to higher valuations (in particular for businesses with high growth in the long term), we would note that the reasons for the long term decline in interest rates strongly suggests that all other things are not equal. Namely deteriorating demographics, low wage growth rates and the persistent failure of inflation to hit central bank targets suggests an environment where earnings growth is more uncertain than previously may have been the case... On the other hand, we would argue that paying more for highly uncertain cashflows from unproven business models makes little sense when the risks to those cashflows is far greater than would have previously been the case.

headline: Passive investing risks systemic capital misallocation as flows inflate mega-cap weights; equal-weighted indices have lagged cap-weighted by 145% on NASDAQ100 since 2015, creating a fragile dynamic that reverses on outflows
reasoning: Spheria argues that the surge into passive funds has inflated the market-cap-weighted indices relative to equal-weighted equivalents — the NASDAQ100 cap-weighted index outperformed its equal-weighted counterpart by 145% since 2015, representing roughly $2.9 trillion of extra value. They liken passive investing to vaccine hesitancy: it works while the majority remains active and keeps markets fundamentally rational, but once passive dominates, price discovery breaks down and capital is misallocated. Historical periods (1929-1953, 1965-1978, 1999-2012) show markets can go sideways for decades, undermining the buy-and-hold passive thesis. Active managers have historically added value at turning points (dot-com, GFC), when passive portfolios were heavily concentrated in subsequently destroyed companies like Citigroup, Bank of America and AIG. Credit Suisse HOLT data shows strategies incorporating operational quality (cash flow return on investment) and valuation generate superior risk-adjusted returns versus momentum/passive strategies through the cycle.
quote: What worries us is that passive investing is akin to avoiding vaccinations. If a small proportion of the population stops getting vaccinated, they are likely to be protected by the herd's immunity. However, if a large portion of the population stops getting vaccinated, they become vulnerable to the virus. Likewise, in passive, it works so long as the majority of money is in active management, keeping the market rational and capital allocation efficient. However, if enough people switch into passive, fundamentals and rational capital allocation is no longer the dominant driver of stock prices.
episode_title: Spheria Global Microcap Fund Monthly June 2020

headline: Exited after 158% AUD gain in March when share price exceeded fundamental valuation; COVID-19 testing boom masks declines in non-COVID test volumes and hot-money risk
reasoning: The fund's top healthcare holding, a diagnostic company, rose 158% in AUD during March after receiving expedited approval to sell its COVID-19 test in the US. The fund exited after the share price exceeded its fundamental valuation, which had already factored in a favourable US roll-out. They also noted that lockdowns have significantly reduced non-COVID diagnostic test volumes, a risk they believe the market has overlooked. They expect hot money will rotate out, providing a re-entry opportunity at a discounted level.
quote: Our top Healthcare stock rose 158% in AUD during March. The diagnostic company in question has been a major beneficiary of COVID-19, and news that it had received expedited approval to sell its COVID-19 test in the USA got the market excited. We exited the position after its share price exceeded our fundamental valuation which factored in a favourable roll-out of the company's products in the US market, the largest diagnostic market globally. In a post-COVID-19 world we could no longer justify the share price, and staying in the position purely to ride the strong share price momentum would be a case of relying on a greater fool theory. Secondly, while COVID-19 testing is lucrative at present, we would hazard a guess that the market has overlooked the impact of lockdowns on the company's remaining portfolio of tests. Industry feedback is that non-COVID diagnostic test volumes have fallen significantly.

They positioned in companies with franchise value, competitive advantage, long-term profitability track records and sustainable balance sheets. Despite this defensiveness, these stocks fell more sharply than expected in February. The fund believes that over the medium to long term their portfolio's valuation and financial metrics will afford relative protection versus weaker, unprofitable competitors who may struggle in a tighter funding environment.
quote: Global share markets began a steep correction in late February with the main trigger being fear surrounding COVID-19 and the follow-on economic impact of counter measures to contain the virus. We believe the ingredients for a correction were in place well before, including extremely rich valuations applied to companies that were conceptually appealing but with limited profitability and in many cases expanding losses. Thus, we positioned in companies with franchise value, some level of competitive advantage and a long-term track record of profitability in conjunction with a sustainable balance sheet - which seemed sensible. However, this did not protect us from market falls and in 'actuality' we saw steeper share price declines in these stock prices in the month of February.

headline: Overweight consumer-facing, media and consumer finance stocks: rent relief, bank forbearance and government funding seen bridging companies to the other side; many have reset cost bases and recapitalised

If the re-opening is faster than anticipated, many will have over-raised and could return capital to shareholders or deploy it at adequate returns.

If the pace of re-opening as we envisage is faster than anticipated, many of the companies will have over-raised thus they will be in an enviable position to return capital to shareholders or deploy capital if returns are adequate.

headline: COVID-19 mortality rate for healthy Australians under 60 is insignificant; re-opening faster than anticipated is the base case, with periodic cluster outbreaks manageable via testing and contact tracing
reasoning: The fund argues that Australia's high per-capita testing rate gives its COVID-19 data greater statistical integrity than most countries, and that any mortality calculation without testing the entire population overstates the true mortality rate. Based on Australian data, the actual mortality rate for healthy people under 60 is insignificant, and no person under 40 has died from COVID-19 in Australia despite high infection levels. The 'flattening the curve' strategy bought time by reducing the infection rate and alleviating hospital pressure, but a second wave of cluster outbreaks is considered likely as the economy re-opens. The fund believes authorities will find a middle ground that allows most locked-down sectors to at least partially re-open, supported by the COVIDSafe app and strengthened testing regimes.
quote: Bearing this in mind and based on the Australian statistical data so far, there is substantive evidence (+4600 positive cases) that the actual mortality rate for healthy people under 60 years of age is insignificant. In fact, no person under 40 years of age has died from COVID-19 in Australia despite high levels of infection. Therefore, the mortality rate under 40 years of age is currently zero... Even in the absence of a vaccine however, we suspect the authorities will find a happy medium that enables most of the sectors impacted by the lockdown to at least partially re-open (albeit likely with modified operating procedures to allow for a modicum of social distancing).

headline: Positioned for faster-than-expected economic re-opening; COVID-19 mortality rate for healthy Australians under 60 is insignificant based on available data, supporting a constructive stance
reasoning: The fund draws a distinction between infection rates (reduced by social distancing) and mortality rates (unaffected by distancing in the absence of treatment advances). Based on Australian data, the mortality rate for healthy people under 40 is currently zero, and for those under 60 it is insignificant. Australia's high per-capita testing gives the data greater statistical integrity. The fund expects periodic cluster outbreaks as the economy re-opens but believes authorities will find a happy medium allowing most locked-down sectors to at least partially re-open. The fund has deliberately positioned for a faster-paced re-opening and concomitant economic recovery.
quote: It's very easy at this point the sharemarket cycle to become overtly bearish given the all-pervading negativity perpetuated in the media (the old adage that bad news sells papers) and the obvious impact on many parts of the economy from the lockdown. Instead of dwelling on these obvious negatives, we believe it is time to be constructive and have purposefully positioned the portfolio for a faster paced re-opening, and concomitant economic recovery whilst also introducing several "growth" companies during the downturn that were previously too expensive to even contemplate. The rotation to recovery names from perceived safety, we believe could pay off handsomely in the medium to long term for our portfolios, given the renewed divergence between growth/defensive stock valuations and pretty much everything else.

The Federal Reserve and other central banks are also to blame, lowering the return on risk-free assets and encouraging yield seeking behaviour. After more than ten years of low interest rates and economic growth it is no surprise that Wall Street has grown complacent.

On that basis we have reduced our position size and are looking for the next MGX type scenario where the risk reward is heavily skewed in our favour.
